rules.title: Net with only one pin
rules.description: Every net needs at least two pins to form a connection.
rules.rationale: A single-member net is usually an unfinished connection or a typo in a signal name.

rules.title: Named pin has no wire
rules.description: A pin carries a signal name but no wire lands on it.
rules.rationale: Uncommitted connections are not built; commit ratsnest lines or remove the name.

rules.title: Wire loops back to the same connector
rules.description: Both ends of a wire are on the same connector.
rules.rationale: Loopbacks are legal (jumpers) but are often unintended; they need a separate jig step.

rules.title: Wire has no route
rules.description: No path of bundle segments connects the two ends of the wire.
rules.rationale: The machine lays wires along segments; a wire without a route cannot be laid or cut to length.

rules.title: Pin assigned to two nets
rules.description: A cavity belongs to more than one net.
rules.rationale: One contact can carry only one signal.

rules.title: Multi-pin net construction not chosen
rules.description: A net with 3 or more pins needs parallel pin-to-pin wires (pins on exactly two connectors, same count on each), a splice, or an explicitly confirmed daisy chain.
rules.rationale: Parallel wires keep one conductor per contact. Two wires in one contact is a specific construction (crimp barrel, sealing, pull test); it must be chosen, not assumed.

rules.title: Contact doesn't match connector or cavity
rules.description: Contact gender must match the connector and contact size must match the cavity.
rules.rationale: A pin contact can't be installed in a socket insert; a wrong-size contact won't seat or seal.

rules.title: Wire gauge outside contact range
rules.description: The wire gauge must be within the crimp barrel range of the contact.
rules.rationale: An out-of-range crimp fails pull test or damages the conductor.

rules.title: Wire too small for net current
rules.description: For nets with a current, the wire rating × derating factor must exceed it.
rules.rationale: Undersized wire overheats in a bundle.

rules.title: Net current exceeds contact rating
rules.description: Net current must not exceed the contact size rating.
rules.rationale: Contacts above rating run hot and lose retention.

rules.title: Twisted pair not on adjacent pins
rules.description: Members of a twisted pair should land on adjacent cavities.
rules.rationale: Untwisted length at the connector reduces noise rejection.

rules.title: Coax/twinax cavity used
rules.description: Size 8/12 shielded contacts are not in the Phase 1 catalog.
rules.rationale: Shielded contacts need their own cable types and termination steps (Phase 2).

rules.title: Bundle doesn't fit backshell clamp
rules.description: The bundle diameter at the connector must fall in the backshell cable-clamp range.
rules.rationale: Too large will not fit; too small will not grip and provides no strain relief.

rules.title: Segment shorter than minimum
rules.description: Segments shorter than the machine minimum cannot be laid automatically.
rules.rationale: The layup head needs room between fixtures.

rules.title: Breakouts too close together
rules.description: Distance between adjacent breakouts must be at least the minimum.
rules.rationale: Closely spaced breakouts cannot be fixtured or finished.

rules.title: Not enough room for bend radius
rules.description: Segments leaving a 90° backshell or breakout need length for a bend of N × bundle OD.
rules.rationale: Tight bends damage insulation and shields.

rules.title: Wire longer than machine maximum
rules.description: Total cut length per wire must not exceed the machine maximum.
rules.rationale: Wire feed and layup travel are limited.

rules.title: Overbraid segment too short
rules.description: Overbraid can't be applied to very short segments.
rules.rationale: The braider needs a minimum run between terminations.

rules.title: Wire shorter than machine minimum
rules.description: Wires shorter than the minimum cut length need manual processing.
rules.rationale: Cut/strip heads need a minimum length to grip.

rules.title: Connector not supported for automated placement
rules.description: Connector series, style and insert must be supported by the machine fixtures.
rules.rationale: Unsupported connectors are placed and loaded by hand.

rules.title: Contact not supported for automated insertion
rules.description: Contacts must be of a size and type the insertion head supports.
rules.rationale: Other contacts are crimped and inserted by hand.

rules.title: Too many connectors for the build plate
rules.description: Number of connectors must not exceed the fixture positions.
rules.rationale: Each connector occupies a fixture position on the build plate.

rules.title: Harness exceeds machine working area
rules.description: The longest end-to-end run must fit the working envelope.
rules.rationale: The layup table has a fixed length.

rules.title: Splice or daisy chain needs manual work
rules.description: Nets with 3+ members need splices or double-crimped daisy chains.
rules.rationale: The machine terminates one wire per contact; splices and double crimps are done by hand.

rules.title: Covering applied by hand
rules.description: Only some covering types are applied by the machine; others are manual steps.
rules.rationale: Manual coverings add labor and lead time.

rules.title: Wire gauge outside cutter range
rules.description: Wire gauge must be within the cut/strip range.
rules.rationale: Heavier gauges are cut and stripped by hand.

rules.title: Bundle diameter exceeds layup limit
rules.description: Bundle outside diameter must not exceed the layup comb.
rules.rationale: Larger bundles can't pass the layup head.

rules.title: Part obsolete, NRND or inactive
rules.description: Parts should be in active production.
rules.rationale: Inactive or obsolete parts have long, unreliable lead times and may not be allowed for new design.

rules.title: Part short of stock
rules.description: Stock must cover the selected order quantity.
rules.rationale: Out-of-stock parts set the ship date.

rules.title: Part lead time exceeds quote tier
rules.description: Part lead time must fit the selected lead-time tier.
rules.rationale: A long-lead part makes the selected tier unachievable.

rules.title: Backshell missing
rules.description: 38999 connectors in a harness need a backshell for strain relief.
rules.rationale: Without a backshell the wires at the grommet carry all the strain.

rules.title: Insert geometry not reviewed
rules.description: Insert cavity positions for this arrangement come from machine extraction and are not yet reviewed.
rules.rationale: Face views, adjacency checks and fixture data depend on cavity coordinates. Unreviewed geometry blocks a ready claim.

rules.title: Reference data not reviewed
rules.description: Catalog fields the build depends on (contact tooling, wire OD/mass, finishing part sizes) must be reviewed, not seed values.
rules.rationale: Seed values are placeholders; a design built on them can't be claimed ready.

rules.title: Dimension not confirmed
rules.description: Segment and drain lengths created from defaults must be entered or confirmed.
rules.rationale: Default lengths are placeholders, not design intent.

rules.title: Part not in catalog
rules.description: Every part number must resolve in the component catalog.
rules.rationale: Unknown parts can't be priced, checked or built.

rules.title: Crimp barrel circular mil area out of range
rules.description: Conductors in each contact or splice barrel, plus CMA build-up, must fall within the barrel's circular mil area window.
rules.rationale: Under-filled crimps pull out; over-filled crimps can't close. Build-up strands bring a light conductor up to the minimum.
rules.paramSource: Seed CMA windows (contact gauge range; splice catalog): verify against the part data

rules.title: CMA reduction (strand removal) used
rules.description: Strands cut from a conductor so it fits a contact barrel.
rules.rationale: IPC/WHMA-A-620 doesn't permit removing strands to fit a crimp: it reduces current capacity and pull strength. Each use is a workmanship exception that needs engineering (and usually customer) approval.

rules.title: Pin neither assigned nor marked no-connect
rules.description: Every cavity needs a decision: a signal, a wired spare, or an explicit no-connect (type NC).
rules.rationale: A blank pin could be a deliberate no-connect or a forgotten signal; marking NC records the intent.

rules.title: Connector missing reference designator
rules.description: Every connector needs a refDes.
rules.rationale: RefDes identifies connectors on the drawing and labels.

rules.title: Duplicate reference designator
rules.description: No two connectors may share a refDes.
rules.rationale: Duplicates make drawings and test programs ambiguous.

rules.title: Net not named
rules.description: Nets still carry an automatic name (NET_001…).
rules.rationale: Signal names make the drawing and test report readable.

rules.title: Label text too long for the label
rules.description: Resolved label text must fit the label's printable length.
rules.rationale: Overlong text is truncated or unreadably small.

rules.title: Covering size doesn't fit the diameter
rules.description: Braid, sleeve and heat shrink must fit the diameter they cover.
rules.rationale: Undersized coverings won't go on; oversized ones won't recover or grip.

rules.title: Band clamp size doesn't fit
rules.description: Band clamp range must contain the diameter under the clamp.
rules.rationale: Wrong-size clamps don't reach tension.

rules.title: Boot size doesn't fit
rules.description: Boot or transition range must contain the diameter at the node.
rules.rationale: Boots must recover onto both backshell and bundle.

rules.title: 360° termination has no band-clamp platform
rules.description: A 360° band-clamp termination needs an EMI backshell with a band platform.
rules.rationale: Without a platform the band has nothing to clamp the shield against.

rules.title: Shield or braid not terminated
rules.description: Each shield or overbraid should be terminated at one end at least; floating ends are flagged.
rules.rationale: An unterminated shield provides no EMI protection.

rules.title: Layer stack order not buildable
rules.description: Layers must be in a buildable order (e.g. a jacket can't be under a braid).
rules.rationale: Some coverings can't be applied over others.

rules.title: Partial layers of the same type overlap
rules.description: Two partial layers of the same type overlap on a segment.
rules.rationale: Overlapping identical layers is usually a mistake and adds diameter.

rules.title: Wire OD outside grommet sealing range
rules.description: Finished wire OD must be within the connector grommet sealing range for the contact size.
rules.rationale: Outside the range the connector won't meet environmental sealing.

rules.title: Finishing step done by hand
rules.description: Potting, splice covers, boots and some coverings are manual operations.
rules.rationale: Manual steps add labor and lead time.

rules.title: Drain not on a ground pin
rules.description: A drain-to-pin termination needs a pin assigned to a ground-class net.
rules.rationale: A drain on a signal pin connects the shield to a signal.

rules.title: Braid coverage below minimum
rules.description: Optical coverage of shields and overbraids must meet the minimum.
rules.rationale: Low coverage reduces shielding effectiveness.

rules.title: Cavity not sealed
rules.description: Each cavity holds one conductor's contact or a catalog sealing plug; flags unsupported cavities, missing plugs, contacts without conductors and double-wired holes.
rules.rationale: Open or double-wired cavities break environmental sealing.
